lesson.summary: Introduction to C: History, Characteristics and Classification
points: Dennis Ritchie developed C at Bell Labs in the early 1970s, building on B in the Unix environment.
C is general purpose, procedural and imperative; it is normally compiled.
Portability needs care with implementation-dependent behavior. Middle-level is an informal classroom label, not an ISO language category.

source_spec.game_concept: A survival strategy set in Shadow Cave – Collapsed Passage, a half-collapsed passage: the lantern keeper must handle glow-eyed lurkers while practicing control flow: while loops. Core idea – Continue Gate: Use continue to skip spoiled lantern oil but keep the loop running.
source_spec.theme: Shadow Cave – Collapsed Passage: a half-collapsed passage
source_spec.core_gameplay_loop: Solve the CP1 stations in the shared Canvas shell while the Week 4 game theme awaits course approval.
secondary_mechanics: Bonus coins for fast correct moves
source_spec.player_objective: C origins: verify archive records c4_l1_q1, c4_l1_q3, c4_l1_q6.
source_spec.controls: Click or press 1–4 to answer; Escape pauses.
source_spec.win_condition: All researched archive facts are correctly identified.
source_spec.lose_condition: skipped_ok drops to 0, or lives reach 0, before the 30-second timer ends.
source_spec.assets_style: Shared Kenney CC0 tile and audio assets with deterministic Canvas layouts; assets are not duplicated per game.
source_spec.duplicate_check_notes: Unique combination of primary mechanic 'Continue Gate' (Week 4 slot 11), mission type 'Survival Siege', and setting 'Collapsed Passage'. No other file shares this combination; games sharing the mechanic differ in mission/win condition and setting, and games sharing the setting use a different mechanic.
